mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 4% in a given month coincides with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discount rates eroding expected equity payoffs.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.0% in a month
failure_condition: Over 60-day rolling window, 20-day forward returns remain non-negative despite persistent FEDFUNDS > 4.0%; or IC > 0.05 in this regime.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in UNRATE by more than 0.2 percentage points is associated with a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return as lower labor-market rigidity supports stronger corporate hiring intentions.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases by >0.2pp in a month
failure_condition: Across 20 consecutive UNRATE up-moves of >0.2pp, 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05); or IC < -0.1.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly expansion in INDPRO above 105 signals increased manufacturing capacity utilization, which precedes a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as firms accelerate capital spending.
regime_hint: Economic expansion with rising capacity utilization
failure_condition: Over a 12-month period with INDPRO > 105, 60-day forward returns are negative on average (mean < 0); or IC < -0.2.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of monthly HOUST above 1100 indicate persistent consumer demand strength, which predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return via higher earnings expectations.
candidate_trigger: HOUST remains above 1100 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: In regimes where HOUST > 1100 for ≥3 months, 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (IC > 0.05); or average return < 0.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in CPIAUCSL below 212.5 (the October 2013 level) coincides with a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as investors anticipate future rate cuts and equity valuations adjust downward.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses below 212.5 in a month
failure_condition: Over 12 months with CPIAUCSL < 212.5, 60-day forward returns remain non-negative (mean ≥ 0); or IC > 0.1.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in PAYEMS below 138,000 coincides with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as elevated unemployment weakens consumer confidence and corporate profit outlook.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS falls below 138,000 in a month
failure_condition: In regimes with PAYEMS < 138,000 for ≥2 months, 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05); or IC > 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both GDPC1 (demand) and RSAFS (retail sales) by at least 3% in the same month predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to dual contraction in economic activity and consumer spending.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 decreases by ≥3% AND RSAFS decreases by ≥3% in a month
regime_hint: Dual contraction in demand and retail
failure_condition: In >80% of such interaction events, 20-day forward returns are non-negative (mean ≥ 0); or IC < -0.15.

mechanism_narrative: During a post-shock recovery regime (defined by UNRATE < 5.5% and FEDFUNDS < 4.0%), a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return is expected as policy remains accommodative and labor market remains weak, supporting equity risk appetite.
failure_condition: In this regime, 5-day forward returns are not positive on average (mean ≤ 0); or IC > 0.1 over a 6-month window.
